summary: Mobile navbar drawer bug REPRODUCED. The drawer opens (opacity animates to 1, pointer-events:auto, body scroll locks), and all 6 mobile links + Book a Demo are technically rendered with data-testids in the DOM. HOWEVER, the drawer element has a computed height of 0px (rect: x:0,y:80,w:390,h:0), so its content is clipped/invisible to real users. Home-page dot-grid overlay intercepts pointer events at the location where the links visually appear to render (they overflow the h:0 container). Playwright's Locator.click() times out with 'dot-grid intercepts pointer events'. Desktop viewport (1440x900) correctly hides the hamburger and mobile drawer and shows the desktop nav.

ui_bugs.issue: Drawer computed height is 0px on mobile, so links/CTA are visually clipped and unclickable. Users tapping the hamburger see nothing change (or see Home page content bleed through since the drawer background never paints).

integration_issues.issue: Click on [data-testid=mobile-nav-link-about-us] does not navigate; Home dot-grid intercepts pointer events because drawer has zero height. Force-clicking the link also does not navigate (URL stays at /).

action_items: Fix Navbar.jsx mobile drawer height. Root cause: the <header> uses `backdrop-blur-md` / `backdrop-blur-xl` (Tailwind => backdrop-filter: blur(...)). Per CSS spec, an ancestor with `backdrop-filter` (or `filter`, `transform`, `perspective`, `will-change: transform`, `contain: paint`) becomes the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants. Because the header element is only 80px tall (h-20), the drawer's `fixed top-20 bottom-0` resolves to top:80 / bottom:0 inside an 80px containing block => height:0.

Recommended fix (choose one): (a) Move the mobile drawer OUT of <header> and render it as a sibling under a React Portal or just below </header> in the JSX so its containing block is the viewport again. (b) Replace `bottom-0` with an explicit viewport height: `h-[calc(100vh-5rem)]` (and drop `bottom-0`). (c) Remove `backdrop-blur-*` from the header while the drawer is open, or move the blur to an inner child div so the header element itself has no backdrop-filter.

After fix, retest: drawer rect should be {y:80, h: innerHeight-80}; tapping mobile-nav-link-about-us should navigate to /about and close the drawer; body.style.overflow should reset to '' after navigation.
critical_code_review_comments: Navbar.jsx: `<div className="absolute inset-0 dot-grid dot-grid-fade opacity-40 pointer-events-none" />` inside the drawer is fine, but is meaningless while parent height is 0. Fix parent height first.

Navbar.jsx: consider portalling the mobile drawer via ReactDOM.createPortal to document.body to make it robust against future ancestor CSS (transform/filter/backdrop-filter) breaking its fixed positioning.

Layout note: `<main className="flex-1">` renders Home content which uses `motion.div` with transform (creates stacking context) - not the primary cause here, but reinforces that portalling the drawer is the safer long-term fix.

success_rate.frontend: 40% (hamburger visible, drawer opens state, desktop hiding all pass; drawer visibility/clickability/navigation all FAIL)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The core bug is `height:0px` on [data-testid=mobile-drawer] because `<header>` has `backdrop-blur-*` which makes header the containing block for the fixed drawer, and header is only 80px tall. Verify with: after tapping hamburger, evaluate getBoundingClientRect() on the drawer -- height must equal (window.innerHeight - 80). Then verify Locator.click on mobile-nav-link-about-us navigates to /about without needing force=True, and document.body.style.overflow returns to '' after the link click.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: viewport 390x844, load /, click [data-testid=navbar-hamburger]. Observed: drawer opacity=1, pointer-events=auto, height=0px. elementFromPoint at About-link center returns a span inside the link, but Playwright still reports Home hero dot-grid intercepts pointer events on click and force-click does not navigate. Root cause: `backdrop-filter` on <header> makes it the containing block for its `position: fixed` child (the drawer). Header height = 80px, so `top:80; bottom:0` collapses to h:0. Mitigation: portal the drawer to body, or use explicit `h-[calc(100vh-5rem)]` on the drawer instead of `bottom-0`.
